about: What a source serves and a caller relays: MSFP Media version 0's fetching (spec/v0/fetching.md) sections 1, 2.1, 2.3, 3, 3.1, 3.2 and 4.2. Sections named alone are fetching's. A carrier's own tickets have no cases here. Generated by tools/vectors from the specification's rules.
mediaNames: file and track names in media URLs (section 1).

names: a name, the URL's path after <stream root><ticket>/, under a ticket the source knows (its kind; for a playback or a download what its answer opened: protocol, subtitles entries, fontCount, the sheet count of the copy's previewLayout, the protocol of each queue entry it prepared, empty for one it didn't, and the bare names its playlists give). valid: served; else 404 (base section 4 names it ticket-refused, for logs; the caller reads the status only), and reason says why (sections 1 and 4.2).
ranges: a Range header against a file of size bytes (section 2.1): start and end, both included, when it is well-formed and satisfiable; reason says malformed or not satisfiable, both answered 416.

fileAnswers: an answer of the source for the file (status and headers; an absent member is an absent header), for the Range the caller sent (none when absent) and the copy's size and etag from the listing, as the caller checks it (sections 2.1, 2.3 and 3.2): valid when it relays it.

relayTypes: what the caller relays as Content-Type (output): the file (what: file) with the copy's mediaType from the listing (value; empty: none), application/octet-stream when it has none; a segment (what: segment) from the source's Content-Type (value) (section 3).

hls: playlists as the caller checks them (section 3.1, steps 1 to 10); reason names the step that fails first. The master playlist's attributes (BANDWIDTH, CODECS, RESOLUTION, VIDEO-RANGE, SUPPLEMENTAL-CODECS, CHANNELS) are the source's to send; no step refuses a playlist without them. The playback of every case has the audio tracks a1 to a40. valid means the checks pass; tags outside the subset may still be dropped before serving. The 2 MiB size and 50,000 URIs are not exercised here.
